concepts.definition: A feeler that turns something around it (temperature, light, sound) into a number.
concepts.example: The light sensor gives a number between 0 (dark) and 255 (very bright).
concepts.pitfall: Thinking the sensor makes guesses; it only gives the value at that moment as a number.

concepts.definition: On the virtual card, you set the sensor value with a slider; the program sees it as a real reading.
concepts.example: When you pull the temperature slider to 35, the program reads 35.
concepts.pitfall: Forgetting to change the slider; the value stays fixed at the start (temperature 21, light 128).

concepts.definition: A sensor block reads the value at the moment it runs; a value that changes afterwards does not change the earlier reading.
concepts.example: Even if you set the temperature to 35 while 21 is scrolling on the screen, the number on the screen stays 21.
concepts.pitfall: Thinking the value will update by itself while the number is scrolling on the screen.

concepts.definition: The boundary value where a decision changes.
concepts.example: In the condition temperature > 30, the threshold is 30; at 31 there is a sad face, at 30 there is not.
concepts.pitfall: Mixing up which side the boundary value goes on; 30 > 30 is false.

concepts.definition: A block that compares a value with the largest value and shows it as the part of the 25 LEDs that fills up from the bottom.
concepts.example: A value of 20 with a largest value of 50 lights up 20 ÷ 50 × 25 = 10 LEDs.
concepts.pitfall: Typing the wrong largest value; if you type 5 for light, the whole screen lights up once the light goes past 5.

concepts.definition: A block that compares two numbers with a sign such as >, < or = and produces true or false.
concepts.example: temperature > 30 is false in a cool room and true in a hot room.
concepts.pitfall: Choosing the sign the wrong way round; if you write <, you see the sad face when it is cool.

quiz.prompt: The temperature is 20 degrees. The block "bar graph temperature up to 50" runs in the program. How many LEDs light up?
quiz.explanation: The ratio is 20 ÷ 50 = 0.4. The bar is spread over 25 LEDs: 0.4 × 25 = 10. The value 20 is less than half (25) of the largest value 50, so less than half the screen lights up.

quiz.prompt: The light level is 64. "bar graph light level up to 255" runs in the program. How many LEDs light up? (Round the result to the nearest whole number.)
quiz.explanation: 64 ÷ 255 is about 0.251. 0.251 × 25 is about 6.27. Because an LED cannot be half on, the nearest whole number, 6, is taken.

quiz.prompt:
The temperature slider is at exactly 30. The A button is pressed.

```
on button A pressed:
  show number temperature
  if temperature > 30 then
    show icon sad face
```

What is seen on the screen?
options: First 30 scrolls, then the sad face comes up
Only 30 scrolls; the sad face does not come up
Only the sad face comes up
quiz.explanation: The show number block scrolls 30. But 30 > 30 is false, because 30 is not greater than itself. So the inside of the if block does not run and the sad face does not come up. You see the sad face at 31; if you want to see it at 30 too, you use ≥.

quiz.prompt:
The light bar always lights up the whole screen, even when the slider is in the middle. The code is:

```
on button B pressed:
  bar graph light level up to 5
```

Where is the bug?
options: The wrong light level block was chosen
The largest value is 5; because light goes up to 255, the largest value should be 255
show number should be used instead of bar graph
The A button should be used instead of the B button
quiz.explanation: The ratio is light ÷ largest, so when the largest value is 5, the ratio goes over 1 as soon as the light goes past 5 and the screen lights up completely. Light goes up to 255, so 255 should be typed as the largest value.

quiz.prompt: You pressed A and the number 21 is scrolling on the screen. While the number is scrolling, you pulled the temperature slider to 35. What happens to this number?
options: It scrolls as 21; 35 does not appear
quiz.explanation: The temperature block reads the value at the moment it runs and prepares the number with that reading. Changing the slider afterwards does not change the old reading. To see 35, you need to press A again.
